purpose: Every shape Conduit invented where no ground truth existed, and the exact evidence that would displace it. This exists because the repository reversed a standing rule: it used to refuse a feature it could not ground, and now it builds one on an educated guess instead. That reversal is only safe if an invention stays distinguishable from a recovery for as long as it lives, and if the arrival of real evidence is an obligation to reimplement rather than an invitation to feel vindicated.
howThisIsEnforced: scripts/verify-conduit-inventions.mjs checks both directions: every CONDUIT-INVENTED marker in the source is registered here, and every entry here still exists in the source. A marker without a Displaced-by line fails. An entry whose displacement evidence has landed fails, which is the point -- the gate turns 'we should revisit this' into a build failure.

markerConvention.inSource: // CONDUIT-INVENTED: <id>\n// Displaced-by: <the capture or document that would settle it>
markerConvention.note: The id is <context>.<Symbol>. It is not a package path, so moving a file does not silently unregister an invention -- renaming the symbol does, which is when someone should be looking at this anyway.

displacementProcedure: When the named evidence lands, record it under docs/evidence/ or docs/reference-platform/ as a normal capture first. An invention displaced by nothing citable is just a different guess.

Reimplement against the evidence. Do not adapt the invented shape to fit -- the invented shape was chosen without constraint and will bend into agreement, which is how a guess becomes an unfalsifiable claim.
Delete the CONDUIT-INVENTED marker and this entry in the same change as the reimplementation, so the register never describes code that no longer exists.
State in the change what the invention got wrong. That is the only feedback anyone gets about how good these guesses are, and without it the next invention is made no better informed than this one.

inventions.what: Native owner-filtered planning-session summary pages with ID seek cursors, exact observed Temporal run ids, a 1000-execution availability bound and explicit CONDUIT_NATIVE tier. Prompts, transcripts, plans and other owners are excluded.
inventions.why: Issue #820 requires discovery of the operator's sessions. No adopted upstream contract defines this index or its pagination, retention and visibility semantics; these are Conduit-owned operational choices over the existing Temporal lifecycle.
inventions.displacedBy: An authoritative planning-session discovery contract defining owner isolation, summary fields, pagination and retained execution visibility.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The native wire shape and bounded indexing strategy may need replacement. Temporal visibility can lag and expire history; this does not establish linearizable inventory, production scale, Hub cancellation, approval or execution authority.

inventions.what: Bounded native operator-documentation retrieval and authorized ontology snapshots with audited, retained source excerpts rendered by the assistant console.
inventions.why: Issue #811 requires grounded answers and rendered citations; no adopted upstream contract defines Conduit retrieval or citation metadata. Sources are server-retrieved records, not model-authored citations.
inventions.displacedBy: An authoritative assistant contract for documentation retrieval, authorized ontology citations and retained source evidence.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The native schema and selected corpus may require replacement. Retrieved excerpts do not prove every answer statement, live deployment state or model accuracy. Read tools confer no write or approval authority.

inventions.what: Conduit-native nullable provider token counts on assistant model provenance, multi-round turn totals, stored conversation messages and the console turn footer. A count is unknown if any round omitted it or the sum overflowed; zero is reported and no missing usage is estimated.
inventions.why: Issue #811 requests model and usage display. The existing HTTP adapter already reads provider counts, but no recovered assistant contract defines a per-turn aggregation or display. This shape carries those observed counts without treating them as complete billing or accounting for unreported retry attempts.
inventions.displacedBy: An authoritative assistant contract for reported per-turn token usage and incomplete multi-round counts.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The optional metadata shape and presentation may need replacement. It adds no model call, cost estimate, budget policy, permission or transcript text; older turn/thread documents remain valid without it.

inventions.what: Conduit-native Organization editors for existing approval-policy and resource-grant APIs, with typed policy variables, revision-bound confirmation and identity-bound request/response handling.
inventions.why: Issue #823 requests confirmed administration through the mounted console. Native Hub contracts already define authority, CEL validation and revision conflicts; no recovered Apollo source establishes a corresponding editing workflow. These controls retain the Hub's decisions and never confer approval themselves.
inventions.displacedBy: An authoritative console workflow for native approval-policy and resource-grant edits.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Presentation may require replacement. No new role, policy language, deletion route or permission is introduced. The Hub authorizes every write; stale revisions fail without automatic retry and observed identity changes discard the editor.

inventions.what: Conduit-native capability-scoped HTTP model name/deadline overrides and separate configured/provider model identities on planning sessions, immutable Accept bindings, audit records and per-call assistant/app-generation provenance.
inventions.why: No adopted upstream contract in this repository defines selection or model provenance for Conduit AI capabilities. A configured alias and provider-reported response id are different facts. Native keys preserve global configuration defaults and share one HTTP endpoint/key; all former global/capability command settings are explicitly refused before HTTP or offline selection.
inventions.displacedBy: An adopted versioned capability-selection and model-provenance contract replacing these native configuration keys and Accept fields.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The keys and additive fields may need replacement. Provider response metadata is not attestation; historical CLI model names remain operator assertions. Missing provider identity stays absent, historical records are not rewritten, and selection adds no approval, publication or deployment authority.

inventions.what: The local Grype report envelope retains provider/package/fix data, selects NVD identifiers and scores, and marks normalization as CONDUIT_NATIVE rather than a Hub artifact assessment.
inventions.why: The pinned public CLI page specifies local execution, NVD preference, CVSS v3/v2 fallback, JSON file output and nonzero-exit behavior, but provides no JSON report fixture or complete tie-break rules. Conduit preserves the Grype envelope with explicit native metadata. NVD scores take priority, then version 3 over 2, then highest score and lexical identifier; zero v3 scores use Grype's Negligible label. Only selected v3 scores remain in the primary CVSS array.
inventions.displacedBy: A sanitized Apollo CLI Grype JSON report establishing output schema, normalization tie-breaks and zero-score severity vocabulary.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The local JSON representation may differ from Apollo's. It is marked native, does not fetch Apollo data, and cannot become an authoritative Hub artifact assessment merely by being produced. The Hub scanner's strict immutable-artifact contract is unchanged.

inventions.what: Apollo-shaped resource identifiers for resources Apollo has published no type token for, minted under ri.conduit.main.<type>.<locator> rather than ri.apollo.
inventions.why: The grammar ri.<service>.main.<type>.<locator> is published, and the service segment names the service that owns the resource -- which is why Autopilot's teams are ri.autopilot and not ri.apollo. A Product that exists only in Conduit is owned by Conduit. Guessing a token inside ri.apollo instead would risk a silent collision: if Apollo's real token for something else matches the guess, two different objects share one identifier and nothing raises a hand. A Conduit-namespaced identifier can only be wrong in the direction of being obviously ours. ADR 0007 left this choice open and this is the answer.
inventions.displacedBy: A published statement giving Apollo's own type tokens for Product, Product Release or Bundle resource identifiers.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low. The identifiers are opaque, self-consistent and unmistakably Conduit's, and every coordinate serving one discloses valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE. If Apollo's real tokens arrive, the values change but nothing was ever claimed to match them.

inventions.what: The locator segment of every Apollo resource identifier Conduit mints: the first 12 bytes of a SHA-256 over a stable input, hex encoded.
inventions.why: The grammar around it is published, not invented -- the pinned OpenAPI carries ri.apollo.main.environment.123, ri.apollo.main.installation.123 and ri.apollo.main.package.123, and ri.autopilot.main.team.123 shows the service segment naming the owning service. Only the locator is open, because Apollo's examples use the placeholder 123. A digest rather than a UUID because the value has to be stable across restarts and replicas without being stored; the one Apollo locator whose format is documented, a Plan's, is a UUID, so this is a known divergence rather than an unconstrained choice.
inventions.displacedBy: A published statement of Apollo's RID locator format, for any resource type Conduit holds.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low in shape, moderate in consequence. The identifiers are opaque and self-consistent, so nothing inside Conduit breaks; but a client that round-trips one into a real Apollo API will not match anything, which is exactly why the coordinates serving them disclose valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE.

inventions.what: The optionality Conduit answers for a Product dependency no publisher declared one for: false, rendered as the string "false".
inventions.why: Neither pinned publish request model carries an optionality input -- PublishHelmChartRequest and PublishServiceRequest both stop at extensions -- so a dependency published on the public Apollo routes arrives with nobody having stated whether it is optional. Conduit's own manifest route can state it, and does, but both paths land in catalog.Dependency.Optional, a plain bool: a declared false and an undeclared one are the same stored value, so the read cannot tell them apart. False is the choice because it is the conservative one for a dependency resolver -- treating an unstated dependency as required refuses a Plan that is missing it, where treating it as optional would silently install without it.
inventions.displacedBy: A published Apollo publish request model carrying dependency optionality, which would let a publisher state it and make the served value theirs rather than Conduit's; or, short of that, a tri-state on catalog.Dependency that keeps an undeclared optionality distinguishable from a declared false all the way to the read.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low. The value is conservative in the direction that fails loudly, and the coordinate discloses valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE so a client is told the answer is Conduit's. A dependency a publisher meant as optional reads as required, which blocks a Plan rather than shipping a broken one.

inventions.what: A per-recipient inbox record carrying its own read state.
inventions.why: Read state is modelled per-recipient because two people notified about the same promotion failure read it independently, and storing readAt on the event would let one of them mark it read for both. Apollo has an inbox -- Hub Settings carries a 'My notifications' page and the tenant viewer role names it -- but no capture shows an entry or its read state.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of Apollo's notification inbox entry and its read state, in particular whether read state is per-recipient.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Medium. Wrong here means the inbox behaves differently from Apollo's, which is visible to operators but not corrupting.

inventions.what: Resolution of one event to its recipients, deduplicated per owner and channel, with current resource-read authority checked before recording fan-out rows and before external submission. Empty nonfuture consent matches no event and preserves the prior inbox.
inventions.why: Deduplication is a judgement, not a recovery: being told the same thing twice in the same place teaches people to ignore it. The channel half of the key is grounded -- Apollo configures email and in-app independently, so reaching one person on both is intended -- but collapsing one owner reached by two preferences on one channel is Conduit's own choice, and Apollo may well fan out per preference instead. Conduit also treats a subscription as interest, not permanent authorization: current native memberships, grants and standing bootstrap policy decide whether it can receive new resource events. External group-only user authority is explicitly unavailable without a trusted current directory; stale subscription claims and the emitting actor are never substitutes. Conduit admits an empty named selection with allFutureTypes=false as explicit off consent. It affects future preference-based fan-out without canceling already selected audiences or queued entries.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of how Apollo resolves one event to its recipients, including deduplication and authorization after permissions change; and a trusted current group-directory integration for background user eligibility.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Moderate availability impact: fail-closed unknown authority can block fan-out or retry a queued delivery. Known refusals are recorded as terminal delivery failures, never as delivered; historical inbox entries are retained.

inventions.what: A private PostgreSQL source-to-notification handoff: the source transaction stores one immutable event and its consent candidates (owner, channel, preference identifier, never contact addresses). A separately leased worker checks current resource-read authority before admitting the event and inbox rows. The first committed event and audience remain immutable on replay, including an empty audience.
inventions.why: A postcommit callback using the request context loses notifications when the request is cancelled, the notification store fails or the process exits between the source commit and recording. Capturing consent through the same SQL transaction makes metadata, audit and the notification obligation succeed or roll back together, including nested savepoints. Re-reading preferences later was rejected because later subscriptions must not receive historical events. Consent is not authorization: delayed admission and external submission still require current authority. Production Hub and packaging-worker startup install the factory before source workers run; admission runs even for IN_APP-only deployments.
inventions.displacedBy: An authoritative source-to-notification durability contract, including source and subscription ordering, consent snapshots, current recipient authority, recovery and retention semantics. No captured Apollo notification API establishes these internals.
inventions.riskIfWrong: This Conduit-native queue adds storage and operational work. An intent write failure rolls back its source transaction before success is acknowledged. Pending work survives restart; finite retries retain exhausted records and reasons rather than claiming delivery. No historical transitions are backfilled. Current denied candidates are excluded at admission, historical inbox rows remain intact, and frozen consent does not promise external delivery after a later preference or contact change.

inventions.what: The rendered form of one inbox entry that a delivery transport sends: a subject line built from the event type and environment, a body of the emitter's summary followed by the event id, type, resource, environment, actor and time, and the destination the recipient's own contact resolved to, which is absent when they hold none.
inventions.why: Something has to decide the wording, and deciding it once in the domain is better than deciding it per adapter, where two transports would phrase the same failure differently and give an operator two facts to reconcile during an incident. Apollo's settings pages establish that email and Slack contacts receive notifications; no capture shows what the message looks like when it arrives, so every choice here -- that the subject leads with the type a subscriber filtered on, that the body repeats the identifiers needed to act without opening a console -- is Conduit's.
inventions.displacedBy: a capture of what Apollo puts in a notification email or Slack post, in particular whether the subject names the event type or the resource
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low and cosmetic in the near term: a wrong subject line is annoying rather than dangerous. It becomes expensive if anyone parses the body, because a downstream receiver built against this shape has to change when the real one arrives. That is why the webhook payload is versioned and structured rather than only textual.

inventions.what: The JSON body Conduit POSTs when delivering a notification to a configured webhook endpoint: a version discriminator, the event and recipient identity the delivery is keyed on, the rendered subject and body, a Slack-compatible text field, and an optional destination object naming the kind and address the recipient's own contact resolved to.
inventions.why: A transport had to exist for the readiness document's Tier 1 gap 1 to close, and a webhook is the one transport Conduit can honestly offer: SMTP needs a recipient address and no store in this repository holds one. Apollo establishes that a team may own a Slack contact and that Slack contacts are deliverable; nothing establishes the request Apollo makes, so the field names, the version discriminator and the decision to duplicate the body into a Slack-shaped text field are Conduit's own.
inventions.displacedBy: a capture of the request Apollo makes when it delivers to a Slack or email team contact, including its field names and headers
inventions.riskIfWrong: Moderate, because this one is on the wire. A receiver written against these field names has to change when the observed request arrives, and a deployment that has pointed a mail relay at this endpoint would keep delivering under the old shape until it did. The version discriminator exists so that change is detectable rather than silent.

inventions.what: The Hub's authenticated notification routes and their request and response shapes: GET /v1/notifications/inbox, GET /v1/notifications/events, GET and PUT /v1/notifications/preferences keyed on the (resource, owner, channel) tuple the store already holds one row for, and GET, PUT and DELETE /v1/notifications/contacts keyed on the (owner, kind) tuple the address book holds one row for. Preference responses, including a missing preference's 404, disclose all known types with no emitter in typesNotYetEmitted and mark complete coverage with typeAvailabilityScope=ALL_KNOWN, distinguishing older selected-only responses. Writes refuse explicit selections of those types; stored legacy preferences remain readable, and opting into all future types retains forward-consent semantics. An empty nonfuture preference records explicit off consent on the existing tuple, retaining its ID and creation time while advancing revision; disabled team consent needs no contact.
inventions.why: The pinned Apollo OpenAPI under docs/reference-platform/snapshots/ publishes no notification operation -- the string does not occur in api-definition.yml -- so there was no published shape to be faithful to. The settings pages captured in docs/evidence/apollo-notification-types.json establish the grain being edited (a per-resource, per-channel preference list, For User or For Team) and nothing else about a wire format, so the routes carry that grain and invent the spelling. Disclosing all unavailable types before saving and refusing explicit unavailable selections prevents subscriptions to silence without removing Apollo's observed vocabulary or damaging legacy records. Retaining silent acceptance was rejected in #840 because a valid type name does not establish a working emitter. Requiring at least one selection made complete unsubscribe and repair of a sole legacy unavailable selection impossible (#905). Off consent remains a resource-authorized, owner-authorized full replacement and grants no new authority.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of Apollo's notification Hub API -- its route paths, its request and response shapes, how it scopes an inbox read to a caller, and how it reports and validates notification types whose emitters are unavailable.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low outside Conduit, moderate inside it. Nothing round-trips these shapes into Apollo, and the routes sit under /v1/notifications where no Apollo-shaped route lives, so a wrong guess cannot collide with a real operation. What a wrong guess costs is a console and any client written against it, which would have to be rewritten when the real shape arrives.

inventions.what: For notification authorization only, an opaque ri.apollo.main.environment RID is matched by forward-computing the existing EnvironmentRID function over the durable native Environment catalog. Exactly one distinct DNS-label Environment identity must match; authority is then checked at environment/<id>. The same resolver is used by preference/event HTTP authorization, background recipient eligibility and requested-resource GET /v1/session capability metadata. Session responses preserve the queried key; mutating route authorization is unchanged. Native resource scopes, stored preference/event identifiers, fan-out joins and delivery identities are unchanged.
inventions.why: The existing apollo.RIDLocator invention makes notification Environment identifiers stable and opaque, while canonical environment:viewer grants are scoped by native Environment ID. Granting authority to the opaque string directly hides that mismatch and cannot reuse ordinary native roles. ListEnvironmentCatalog already projects accepted desired state and persisted Agent report identities. Looking up the forward mapping against that source avoids decoding an opaque digest, trusting Event.Environment, inventing a second grant hierarchy or migrating stored subscriptions. Unknown, invalid and ambiguous aliases fail closed; inventory lookup failures remain errors for background delivery rather than authorizing an uncertain recipient.
inventions.displacedBy: An authoritative notification resource-to-authorization mapping, including Environment identity aliases, native grant scope, ambiguity handling and lifecycle semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: This is a Conduit-native authorization boundary, not an Apollo protocol claim. It does not rewrite or backfill stored keys. A missing trusted catalog identity prevents opaque-RID access and delivery until that identity exists; native scopes retain their original policy. A changed mapping must be replaced deliberately while preserving existing event and subscription identities.

inventions.what: A stored destination per (owner, kind) -- an address, its kind, an opt-into-future-resources flag and its timestamps -- where the owner may be a TEAM or a USER, and an identifier minted as a digest over (owner, kind) rather than chosen or derived from the address.
inventions.why: Apollo establishes the team half: a contact is created in Hub Settings, has one of three kinds, is what a resource selects, and a team holding none receives nothing. It establishes no user contact at all, and may well have none -- a tenant's account email would do the same job. Conduit needs one anyway, because its preference model already admits a USER owner on the EMAIL channel and without an address that subscription reaches nobody, which is precisely the Tier 1 readiness gap this closes. Keying on (owner, kind) rather than on a contact identifier follows the dialog, which creates a contact of a kind for an owner; the identifier is derived from the same tuple so every replica mints it without storing it, and deliberately not from the address, because an identifier derived from an address carries the address wherever it travels and changes identity when somebody moves.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of Apollo's contact API -- what a contact is keyed on, whether a user holds one at all, what it is called, and what its identifier looks like.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Moderate, and the highest-consequence entry in this register, because the value stored is personal data. Being wrong about the shape costs a migration. Being wrong about the authorization would cost somebody their mail, which is why the owner check admits no administrator override and is held down by TestThroughTheHubOnePrincipalCannotWriteAnotherPrincipalsContact rather than by this paragraph. A user contact that Apollo turns out not to have is a table Conduit stops writing, not a value anyone round-trips into Apollo.

inventions.what: The rule that turns one recipient into one destination at delivery time: skip contacts belonging to another owner, skip an in-app recipient entirely, skip any kind Apollo does not deliver to, prefer the kind whose name matches the channel, break remaining ties by kind name, and resolve to nothing when no contact qualifies -- which leaves the operator-configured endpoint as the fallback.
inventions.why: Something has to choose, because Apollo publishes two per-resource channels (EMAIL, IN_APP) and three contact kinds (EMAIL, SLACK, PAGERDUTY), and the two vocabularies overlap in exactly one place. What is grounded: PagerDuty receives nothing, so it is never a destination; an in-app entry is delivered by the inbox, so an address would send it somewhere its owner never chose. What is Conduit's: that a team whose only contact is Slack is reached there rather than not at all, that ties break by kind name so two replicas resolving at the same moment agree, and that a recipient with no contact falls back rather than failing. A failed read of the address book is deliberately not folded into 'no contact' -- that retries, because delivering to the fallback on a failed query would send a person's notification somewhere they did not choose.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of how Apollo chooses which of a recipient's contacts a notification is delivered to, and what it does when the recipient has none.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Moderate. Wrong here changes where a notification lands rather than what is stored, and the fallback bounds the worst case at the behaviour that existed before contacts: a deployment that records no contacts is bit-for-bit unchanged. The direction that would cost most is preferring a kind Apollo would not have, which is why the kind is on the wire beside the address so a receiver can refuse one it does not expect.

inventions.what: Which of Apollo's two observed recall notification event types Conduit raises for a given recall: PRODUCT_IN_OPEN_ENDED_RECALL when the recall has no ending version and is not single-version, and PRODUCT_RECALLS otherwise.
inventions.why: Both labels are observed, in docs/evidence/apollo-notification-types.json, and so are their descriptions -- 'Future releases of this Product will be recalled' for the first, 'Anytime a bug or critical issue has been discovered in my product' for the second. A Conduit recall with no upper bound covers every version the Product will ever publish above its starting version, which is the first description exactly. What is not established is that Apollo distributes the two this way: the same capture records, as an upstream ambiguity, that nothing says whether these are two types or one type rendered at two granularities. Raising only one of them was the alternative, and it would have told a subscriber who ticked the other that no recall had opened.
inventions.displacedBy: a capture showing which notification event type Apollo raises for a recall with an ending version, against one without
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low, and reversible in one function. Nothing leaves Conduit under these type names except a notification a Conduit deployment delivers to its own configured transport, and both names are Apollo's own, so a wrong split mislabels an inbox row rather than inventing a vocabulary. What it costs is a subscriber who ticked exactly one of the two: they see the recalls Conduit routed to their type and not the others, which reads as no recall having opened.

inventions.what: Which Governance writes raise which of Apollo's observed notification event types, and on what resource: CHANGE_REQUEST_PENDING_APPROVAL on the request's Environment each time a change request is committed waiting for an approver (once per review round, keyed on the request id and revision), and ROLE_CHANGE on the resource a grant names each time a resource grant's relationship, roles or operations change. RBAC_CHANGE is raised by nothing.
inventions.why: Both type labels are observed, in docs/evidence/apollo-notification-types.json, and nothing captured says what triggers either or who receives it. Leaving them unraised was the state #840 records: an approver was never told a request was waiting. The Environment is the subscription grain because it is the identifier Conduit already publishes and the one the existing recall and reconciliation events join on; reviewer requirements name roles and teams, and resolving those to recipients here would be a second fan-out rule beside notifications.Fan. A grant is a write against exactly one resource, which matches the per-resource page ROLE_CHANGE was observed on; raising RBAC_CHANGE for the same write would assert the two are one event, which the capture does not establish.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of which resource Apollo raises CHANGE_REQUEST_PENDING_APPROVAL and ROLE_CHANGE on, who receives each, and what separates ROLE_CHANGE from RBAC_CHANGE.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low, and reversible in one adapter. Nothing leaves Conduit under these names except a notification a deployment delivers to its own transport. What a wrong choice costs is reach: an approver who is not subscribed to the Environment is still not told. RBAC_CHANGE has no emitter; legacy selections remain readable and disclosed by typesNotYetEmitted, while new explicit selections are refused rather than promising grant-change notifications on that type.

inventions.what: What counts as a failed promotion for PRODUCT_RELEASE_PROMOTION_FAILED -- a stored evaluation whose lifecycle is ABORTED (evaluation window timed out, a canary recall condition triggered, or an operator aborted the run), and not one that is merely BLOCKED or was CANCELLED -- and the resource the event is raised on, product/<coordinate>.
inventions.why: The type label is observed on a Product's settings page and its prose name is 'Promotion failures'; nothing captured says which outcome raises it. A staged promotion is BLOCKED on every evaluation until its soak elapses, so raising on BLOCKED would notify on a stage working as designed and teach subscribers to ignore the type. ABORTED is the one lifecycle in which the run is over and the Release did not cross the channel boundary without a person choosing that. Conduit mints no ri.apollo.main identifier for a Product, so the event uses the identifier Governance authorizes a Product by, which is the one a preference can be authorized on.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of what Apollo counts as a failed promotion for PRODUCT_RELEASE_PROMOTION_FAILED and which resource identifier the event carries.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low. A wrong outcome rule changes how often an inbox row appears, not any stored promotion record. A wrong resource identifier is the costlier half: a preference set on some other spelling of the Product matches nothing, silently, and would have to be re-keyed when a published Product identifier arrives.

inventions.what: A `facets` object on GET /v1/fleet/installations counting installations per value of environment, product, health, rolloutStatus, configStatus and lifecycle, where each dimension's count is computed with that dimension's own filter excluded from the query.
inventions.why: The console needed a faceted filter rail, and the Hub already served per-dimension counts as `summary`. `summary` is computed after the whole query is applied, so once health=UNHEALTHY is selected every other health bucket reads zero -- a control that says "HEALTHY 0" beside a fleet that is mostly healthy. Excluding a dimension from its own facet is the conventional resolution and the only one under which the number beside a filter answers the question the click asks: how many rows would I get if I picked this instead. The alternative considered was serving `summary` unchanged and labelling the rail "within the current selection", which needs no invention and was rejected because it makes the rail unusable for navigation -- every unselected sibling reads zero, so there is nothing to navigate to. What is NOT established is that Apollo serves such a shape at all: the pinned OpenAPI snapshot publishes no fleet-installation filter-count operation, and the 2020 screenshot in docs/ui/evidence/legacy-apollo-2020/ shows a rail with counts and proportional bars without showing what the counts are computed over. The key names are Conduit's own query parameters, deliberately, so that a facet cannot be served under a name the filter would not accept.
inventions.displacedBy: a capture or published schema showing Apollo's own fleet/installation filter-count response -- its field names, and whether a selected dimension is excluded from its own count
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low and reversible in one function plus one console component. Nothing leaves Conduit under this shape except the console's own read of its own Hub; the surrounding `summary`, `installations` and pagination fields are untouched, so a client that ignores `facets` is unaffected. The failure mode if the exclusion semantics are wrong is a rail whose counts do not match the result an operator then gets, which the rail's own labelling addresses by stating what each count is over. Authorization is not at risk: facet contributions pass the same per-Environment read check as rows, so no count discloses an Environment the caller may not read.

inventions.what: The scan-freshness window an ArtifactSecurityPolicy enforces when it states none: seven days, applied as a floor rather than as an off switch, so a policy requiring PASS can no longer accept evidence of unbounded age.
inventions.why: That freshness was optional was the residue #54 named, and closing it required choosing a number nothing establishes. What is grounded is the direction, not the value: Apollo's own material describes continuous rescanning that catches vulnerabilities discovered after a Release passed, which only means anything if a passing scan expires. Seven days was chosen for the shape of its failure modes rather than for any evidence -- exceeding it costs a rescan wherever a scanner is configured, so too tight costs latency while too loose restores the defect. A day was rejected because on a Hub with no scanner configured it fails closed daily, and a floor that reads as breakage gets switched off.
inventions.displacedBy: a published statement of the scan-freshness window Apollo applies when a security constraint names none
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low and bounded by configuration. Wrong here means Conduit rescans on a different cadence from Apollo, which any Environment can correct by stating maximumScanAgeSeconds explicitly; nothing on the wire carries the value and no stored shape depends on it. The one deployment it can disturb is a Hub running a PASS policy with no scanner and evidence older than a week, which is refused where it was previously admitted -- intended, and the reason the number is not tighter.

inventions.what: A Conduit-native append-only promotion run with RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, ABORTED and CANCELLED phases, exact predecessor continuation and a durable terminal reason, separate from PASSED/BLOCKED eligibility.
inventions.why: The pinned public release-channel documentation and changelog establish in-progress, succeeded and aborted promotions and cancellation reasons, but publish no lifecycle API shape or transition contract. Keeping immutable evaluations in a predecessor chain preserves existing eligibility replay and provides atomic terminal transitions without rewriting prior decisions.
inventions.displacedBy: A published Apollo promotion lifecycle API schema and transition contract, including cancellation reasons.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Medium. Run identifiers, phase wire tokens and continuation requests may differ from Apollo. They are served only on Conduit-native v1 routes with CONDUIT_NATIVE disclosure; published Apollo transport schemas remain unchanged.

inventions.what: A first-class SLACK channel for native v1 resource preferences, inbox fan-out and channel-specific delivery.
inventions.why: Public notifications documentation establishes Slack delivery and captured team contacts establish the Slack destination kind, but the captured resource settings only show email and in-app preference lists. inventions.what: A workspace review target identity bound to native actor/delegation, environment, workspace, revision and source coordinates; submission always uses the existing mandatory-human-review command.
inventions.why: The existing native target used only workspace ID and revision and allowed policy auto-approval before a later service-layer rejection. There is no public private-workspace submission identity or delegated-author transport establishing these details.
inventions.displacedBy: a published or authorized sanitized workspace submission identity, delegated-author and mandatory-human-review contract.
inventions.riskIfWrong: This is a native review-only proposal, not execution or deployment. Service-account and one-hop represented identity are retained for the existing self-review rule. Previously stored requests are not rewritten.

inventions.what: Conduit-native same-origin SSE delivery with opaque owner/delegate/grant-bound cursors, single-owner durable journal, native per-resource visibility and demand-driven outbox refresh. Verified retained-source gaps atomically retire every delivery epoch and require authorized catch-up before rebaselining.
inventions.why: ADR 0016 chooses this console transport and event vocabulary. No recovered Apollo protocol establishes a general operator event stream or these cursor, eligibility and storage semantics. The implementation uses existing native read decisions and does not infer a private upstream wire contract. Bounded native retention requires an explicit reset rather than silently skipping missing source positions.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or owner-approved sanitized event-stream contract establishing transport, cursor binding, stream eligibility, source coverage and resource authorization semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Native event/cursor and transport shapes may need replacement. This is an explicit Conduit extension, conveys no approval/execution authority, and the console reconciles subscriptions through existing authorized reads with polling fallback. The bounded Audit feed is session observation, not durable event history; KPI counts cover loaded authorized snapshots.

inventions.what: Conduit-native read-only release view joining native fleet desired/reported installation facts, environment-scoped declared Product promotion graph edges, and fully authorized process-local staged rollout waves.
inventions.why: Issue #415 requests a combined backend contract. Existing native fleet, Product settings and staged rollout records establish the underlying facts; no recovered public or authorized Apollo source establishes this combined route or JSON projection.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or owner-approved sanitized release rollout view contract establishing join grain, Product and Environment visibility, promotion graph scope and wave persistence semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The JSON projection may need replacement. It is observation-only, not rollout or promotion authority. Mixed-visibility rollouts are omitted entirely; empty observations remain unknown. The wave store is process-local and reads across sources are not a transaction.

inventions.what: A Hub-routed workspace coding-agent ACP endpoint scoped to one authenticated operator and workspace branch, mapping low-risk ACP permission requests to explicit owner Confirm and high-risk requests to mandatory-human-review Change Requests, while mirroring redacted editor activity onto the console AG-UI stream.
inventions.why: The ACP wire protocol (@agentclientprotocol/sdk@2.6.0, protocolVersion 1) and AG-UI 1.0 event envelopes are public contracts, whereas how a Conduit Hub routes workspace editor ACP turns, classifies governed permission risk tiers, and correlates sessionId/runId/threadId across audit and console streams is unestablished in public Apollo sources.
inventions.displacedBy: a published or authorized sanitized workspace coding-agent ACP transport, governed permission mapping, and console activity projection contract.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Marked CONDUIT_NATIVE; actual file and terminal callbacks require fresh governed decisions. Transport HTTP egress filtering does not confine direct filesystem or network access by spawned agent/terminal processes. Risk-pattern matching is not an OS sandbox. The Node implementation remains draft pending enforced isolation/egress and workspace identity/branch integration evidence; no complete offline or production-governance guarantee is established.

inventions.what: Three optional fields on a Release's deployable artifact (the existing chart coordinate): kind (helm-chart by default, zarf-package or uds-bundle), architectures (exactly one platform), and packageName, the Zarf package name the artifact deploys as. A package kind is addressed by repository and sha256 digest only; a tag is refused.
inventions.why: The pinned Apollo publication models carry Helm charts and services and state no Zarf or UDS artifact. Without a declared kind the Spoke's Zarf/UDS executor derived an OCI reference from the Product name, and nothing told a reviewer or the Spoke which tool a step would run. The existing coordinate was extended, rather than a second artifact added, so that scanning coverage, availability evidence, registry assignment and Bundle transfer cover a package by the rules they already apply to a chart.
inventions.displacedBy: a published or owner-approved Product Release contract that states how a Zarf package or UDS bundle artifact, its architectures and its deployed package name are declared.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The field names and reuse of the chart coordinate may need replacing. Absent fields preserve Helm documents and digests. The Hub checks selected packages against the operator-declared Environment packageArchitecture, and the Spoke independently checks its configured target. Multiarchitecture declarations are refused; a falsely declared OCI index still fails exact deployed-digest readback. The Apollo manifest routes cannot publish a package kind.

inventions.what: A ConfigMap named conduit-applied-<zarf package name>, written by the Spoke in the step's namespace after a Zarf or UDS deploy has succeeded and been read back. It holds the Release digest, version, config digest, a digest of the exact variables passed, the artifact digest, and the digest and generation Zarf recorded for that deploy. The Spoke reports a configuration as APPLIED, and a Release or config digest at all, only from this record and only while its Zarf digest and generation match what Zarf currently holds.
inventions.why: Legacy Zarf state lacks deployment variables. Zarf v1.0.0 now records a DeployConfig snapshot, partially displacing that limitation, but it does not identify the Conduit Release or the parent UDS Bundle. The executor retains its generation/digest-bound applied record for that mapping and legacy deployments; this is not a claim that v1.0.0 lacks variable evidence. Reading native DeployConfig for configuration convergence remains separate work.
inventions.displacedBy: a Zarf or UDS release that records the variables and source reference a deployment was given in its own deployed-package state, or a published contract for reading them back.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The record is the Spoke's account of its own action, not a read of live configuration: changes made underneath the package without a Zarf deploy are not detected, and anyone who can write ConfigMaps in the namespace can write it. For a bundle only the one named package is bound. A reader between the delete and the create sees no record and reports INDETERMINATE.

inventions.what: A Hub-side deny-list for Agent client certificates: a revocation record with scope SERIAL (one certificate), AGENT (one Environment/Agent identity) or ENVIRONMENT (every Agent of an Environment), a deterministic arv_ identifier derived from what is revoked, and a notBefore instant under which an identity or Environment revocation refuses certificates issued at or before it and admits ones issued after. Enforced on every route registered DecisionAgent, failing closed with 503 when the list cannot be read.
inventions.why: #847: the Hub authenticated an Agent by a client certificate and had no way to cut one off short of replacing the CA. The pinned Apollo sources describe agents authenticating to the Hub and do not describe a revocation record, its scopes, its identifier or its re-enrolment rule. X.509 has CRL and OCSP, which need an issuer-run service this repository does not ship and cannot assume; this is the smallest control the Hub can enforce by itself.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo agent credential revocation record defining its scope, identifier and re-enrolment semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The record schema, scope vocabulary and the notBefore re-enrolment rule would need a migration. The rule decides on a timestamp the issuer wrote: an issuer that backdates NotBefore or whose clock trails the Hub's yields a replacement that stays refused until the instant passes, and a replacement issued for the same private key readmits the key's holder. Both are stated in docs/operations/agent-enrolment.md. Revocation removes no authority from operators and is not a substitute for CA rotation when the CA itself is compromised.

inventions.what: Conduit-native routes under /v1/environments/{environmentID}: GET and POST agent-revocations, DELETE agent-revocations/{revocationID}, and GET agent-credentials, which reports the last certificate each Agent presented (serial, validity, last seen, seconds until expiry, and the revocation that would refuse it).
inventions.why: #847 requires the revocation control to be operable and audited, and requires certificate expiry to be visible per Agent without labelling a metric by tenant. No Apollo management wire for agent credentials is recovered. The routes reuse existing authority rather than inventing a role: manage-permissions on the Environment to change the deny-list, read on the Environment to see it, both through Governance's audited resource decision; each change is also written to the authorization audit trail as configureInfra.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo agent credential management API establishing revocation routes, body shapes and authority.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Routes, body shapes and the choice of manage-permissions as the bar would need migration. The surface exposes certificate serials and validity to Environment readers and never key material. A removal whose audit record cannot be written is undone; an addition whose record cannot be written stays in force and is reported as a failure.

inventions.what: The conduit agent-credential command group: list, revocations, revoke (--serial, --agent-id or --all-agents, with --not-before and a required --reason) and unrevoke.
inventions.why: #847 asks for an operator control, and the pinned CLI command contract has no agent credential commands. The group is a projection of identity.AgentRevocationHTTPSurface through the existing operator HTTP adapter and adds no authority of its own.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo agent credential management CLI contract defining command paths, arguments and revocation semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Command paths and flags would be renamed. The CLI validates a revocation locally with the same domain function the Hub uses, so a divergence between them is a compile-time dependency rather than a second copy of the rule.

inventions.what: The reference EXTERNAL_MATERIAL_PREPARER executable shipped in the Agent image: the kubernetes-secret://NAME provider-reference grammar, projection of requested keys from a source Secret in one Environment-owned namespace into a Secret in a managed namespace, image pull Secrets from a dockerconfigjson source, ownership by the app.kubernetes.io/managed-by label and platform.delivery/material-* annotations, and exit statuses 1 to 7 as the failure vocabulary.
inventions.why: #848: the Agent delegated registry and secret material to an Environment-owned executable and no implementation shipped, so every tenant had to write one. The Agent's side of the contract (internal/agent/material.go) is Conduit's own and fixes only the request; nothing recovered establishes how Apollo resolves a provider reference inside an Environment. A Kubernetes-native provider needs no dependency and composes with External Secrets Operator or any other controller that materialises a Secret.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo agent secret-provider contract defining how an Environment resolves registry credentials and installation secrets.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The reference grammar, the ownership metadata and the exit statuses are this implementation's and would change. The preparer keeps no history, so a rollback restores from whatever the previous reference names now; it declines image pre-pull rather than claiming it; and it acts with the Agent's ServiceAccount, so it adds no isolation between the Agent and the material it handles. ESO and Vault integration is by composition and has not been exercised.

inventions.what: The Hub route POST /v1/mcp: stateless Streamable HTTP speaking MCP 2025-11-25, serving the assistant's two read tools (query_ontology_objects, review_change_diff) as the authenticated operator, each call audited with origin mcp and bounded at 8 KiB.
inventions.why: #815 asks for the assistant's read tools to be reachable from an MCP client. Nothing recovered establishes that Apollo exposes an MCP surface or what it would carry, so the tool names, argument shapes and result payload are the assistant tool port's own and the endpoint adds no authority: it reuses the assistant's read-only mode allowlist, its argument validation, authorization as the caller and its per-call audit.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo MCP or agent-tool contract defining tools, transport and authority.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The route, the tool names and the result shape would change and MCP clients configured against it would need reconfiguring. The surface is read-only, so a wrong guess cannot have changed state; review_change_diff is readable by any authenticated operator, which is the assistant's existing rule and would be inherited by any replacement unless tightened there.

inventions.what: The conduit-eval command and its files under docs/evidence/model-evals: the corpus schema (cases, capabilities, assertion kinds), transcripts keyed by the sha256 of the prompt bytes, the score report keyed by model id, prompt digest set and skill digest, the five score dimensions, and the replay gate rule (no unrecorded prompt, no score below the committed baseline).
inventions.why: #814 requires an offline-first way to detect prompt and skill changes and to score a model on the planning and packaging prompts. No Apollo evaluation contract is recovered; the planning and packaging prompts are Conduit's own, so their evaluation format is too. The harness drives the product's planner and package writer rather than a copy of their prompts.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo model evaluation contract defining cases, scoring and gating.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The corpus, transcript and score formats and the dimension names would be replaced and every baseline re-recorded. The committed baseline is a canned offline agent's, so no decision about model quality rests on these files today; the risk is a gate that pins prompt digests under names that later read as quality scores.

inventions.what: An optional packageArchitecture on the native desired-state Environment, required when selecting a Zarf package or UDS bundle, admitting only matching package declarations with one architecture and excluding incompatible channel candidates.
inventions.why: Issue #833 requires architecture admission before approval. No Environment runtime capability or discovered architecture currently exists. An explicit operator declaration is narrower than guessing from Hub hardware, labels, or Spoke enrollment; the Spoke independently checks its actual configured target.
inventions.displacedBy: a published or owner-approved Environment capability contract establishing package target architecture and its admission semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: This is a Conduit-native operator declaration, not cluster discovery or proof that all nodes share an architecture. A misdeclared target is still refused by the Spoke before execution. Clusters with mixed architectures and OCI index-to-platform resolution remain unsupported; the omission preserves existing Helm desired-state documents.

inventions.what: Conduit-native assistant packaging cancel/rerun proposals bind the source digest, proposal revision, target installation/Product/Environment and tool/template versions under conduit.assistant-action/v1. Independent approval dispatches a shared audited packaging command and exposes command acknowledgement separately from observed run termination. Same-decision recovery uses a durable execution claim and deterministic successor workflow identity. Eval feedback and Change Request review have explicit native action rules.
inventions.why: The generic assistant PLAN intent records had no executor and could not safely authorize a later worker mutation. Existing Conduit packaging controls establish the implementation and audit boundary; no Apollo assistant execution contract is present. Unsupported actions are removed from the assistant schema rather than advertised as inert writes.
inventions.displacedBy: a published or authorized sanitized assistant action execution contract covering run binding, approval, command receipts and recovery.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Moderate within Conduit: clients must adapt to the smaller action allowlist and unsupported writes now return TOOL_INVALID. Unattended dispatch requires current server-owned membership and refuses delegated or group-only author authority. Repeated cancellation requests are idempotent worker requests, not a claim of exactly-once external effects or completed termination.

inventions.what: Optional native PlanRecord decisionTraceparent, lease-span links and Agent execution parentage outside Plan identity.
inventions.why: W3C trace context and OTLP define telemetry transport, not Conduit Plan persistence or asynchronous polling linkage. The maintainer selected this opt-in native design in ADR 0018.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized protocol defining persisted Plan decision trace context and asynchronous lease linkage.
inventions.riskIfWrong: A different downstream trace-link contract would need a versioned diagnostic metadata adaptation; tracing must never change Plan identity or authority.

displaced.whatTheInventionGotWrong: Its premise. The entry said Conduit 'carries the Environment where Apollo's documented example carries a Space'. Apollo's documented example carries no Space: the pinned OpenAPI publishes aeid:apollo-environment-demo:helm-chart:wordpress twice, beside environmentRid, and that second segment is an environment name. Conduit's aeid:<environment>:helm-chart:<entity> matches the published example in segment count, in the helm-chart product-type token, and in the meaning of the second segment. Nothing was invented; the construction was recovered and then filed as a guess.
displaced.howThisWentWrong: The grammar record's own conduitBearing already said the space-or-environment question was NOT established, and the invention entry -- written after reading it -- asserted it was a Space anyway. That is an inference hardening into a fact across two files in one day. The answer was in a snapshot this repository has held since the OpenAPI was pinned; nobody had compared the OSDK example against the OpenAPI example. The OSDK's 'mojito' says nothing about what it is, which is exactly why it should not have been read as saying 'Space'.
displaced.note: ApolloEntity.id still discloses valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE, and that is unchanged and correct: no Apollo Hub answered with the string, Conduit composed it from its own environment and entity names. Serving a value built to a published shape is still serving a value Conduit built.

displaced.whatTheInventionGotWrong: It existed at all. Apollo's notification subscriptions carry no severity: filtering is by type and channel, and nothing on any notification page or screenshot has a severity, priority or urgency control. The invention also named a displacement condition -- 'a capture establishing Apollo's MonitoringSeverity enum members' -- that could never have displaced it, because this repository's own reference note already records MonitoringSeverity as a Foundry Data Health type rather than an Apollo one. An invention whose stated evidence cannot settle it is unfalsifiable, which is the failure the register exists to prevent and which the register itself shipped.
displaced.note: Apollo does have a severity, on the Environment Events surface, where the 2020 capture shows the facet Success/Info/Warning/Error. That is a different surface and is not modelled here. Note also that the invented members -- INFO, WARNING, ACTION_REQUIRED, CRITICAL -- match neither that vocabulary nor its ordering.

displaced.whatTheInventionGotWrong: Every name, and worse, the shape. All eight invented kinds are gone; nine observed types replace them, and not one invented name survived. The structural error was closing the set: Apollo's documentation says the supported types 'will grow over time', and the settings page carries a per-resource, per-channel toggle reading 'If enabled, you will opt into future notification types added for this resource'. Apollo solved openness with forward consent. The invention closed the vocabulary and justified it by analogy to the Change Type taxonomy -- reasoning from a neighbouring design instead of looking, which is exactly how a closed set becomes the thing that silently drops every type added later.

The grain and three whole dimensions. Apollo's unit is a preference per (resource, principal, channel), not one subscription filtered by kind and severity. Missing entirely: delivery channels, team contacts as a prerequisite for a team receiving anything, and the two opt-into-future toggles. Present and wrong: a severity floor Apollo does not have, and a Muted boolean where Apollo's mute vocabulary belongs to monitors. The one part that held was ownership by user or team, which was the one part grounded in recovered evidence rather than guessed.

howThisWentWrong.note: All three displacements landed the day after the register was written, from evidence that was already in reach. This is recorded because the register's value depends on its guesses being honest ones, and these were not -- they were made without looking.
whatWasAvailable: Three public Palantir documentation pages under managing-notifications, already listed in docs/reference-platform/public-documentation-manifest.tsv with their content digests.

Five screenshots on those pages, already counted by docs/reference-platform/IMAGE-DERIVED-GAPS.md, which dispositioned the section 'Boundary' without opening them -- in a document whose own thesis is that screenshots are where a UI-first product states its enum values.
docs/ui/evidence/legacy-apollo-2020/environment-events.webp, committed in this repository, showing the Events severity and category facets.
howThisWentWrong.whyItWasNotSeen: docs/reference-platform/reference/notifications.md opened with 'No public Palantir docs page was captured for this capability'. That sentence was false against this repository's own manifest, had never been checked against it, and was taken at face value. The gate added in scripts/verify-documentation-claims.mjs now checks exactly this class of claim, because it is the cheapest possible check and nothing was doing it.
howThisWentWrong.lesson: The register asks whether an invention is marked and whether it names what would displace it. It does not ask whether the invention was necessary. A guess made without exhausting the sources already in the repository is not an educated guess, and marking it does not make it one.
